candidate_plain_language_facts: The Fed raised its policy rate range to 2.25 to 2.50 percent and anticipated further increases.
It cited pandemic supply and demand imbalances, higher food and energy prices, and the war in Ukraine as inflation pressures.
It reaffirmed its longer-run 2 percent inflation objective; this was a goal, not a promise of next-year inflation.

candidate_plain_language_facts: The Fed kept its policy rate range at 5.25 to 5.50 percent.
It said inflation had eased over the previous year but remained elevated.
It did not expect a rate cut to be appropriate until it had greater confidence that inflation was moving sustainably toward 2 percent.
